elements.element: The licence extends automatically to Customer's affiliates without a written-notice condition.
elements.evidence: The grant covers only affiliates “designated by written notice,” so affiliate coverage is conditional rather than automatic.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no licence grant or permitted-use right for contractors.
No language states that any paid-up licence is perpetual.
No language states that any paid-up licence is irrevocable.

elements.element: Subscription licences may be terminated only for an uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no restriction limiting termination of subscription licences to uncured material breach.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to successors generally.
elements.evidence: Transfer without approval is permitted only to “a successor in a merger or acquisition,” not to successors generally.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered upon written notice.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly extends to Client's “affiliates designated by written notice.”

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: Section 15 permits assignment by Client “to a successor in a merger or acquisition” without the other party's approval.

result.reason: The operative redline fully reaches the fallback by covering designated affiliates on written notice and permitting assignment to an M&A successor without approval. It does not reach the preferred position because it omits contractor rights, perpetual and irrevocable treatment for paid-up licences, and the required subscription-termination limitation, while affiliate and successor coverage remain narrower than preferred. The changes are limited to the fallback requirements and do not disturb unrelated commercial terms.
